title: Bhikkhus, when a child grows up and his faculties mature, he enjoys the full range of the five strands of sensual pleasure — forms cognizable…
content: Bhikkhus, when a child grows up and his faculties mature, he enjoys the full range of the five strands of sensual pleasure — forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, stimulating sensual desire, enticing; sounds... odors... flavors... tangibles... When he sees a form with the eye, he lusts after a pleasant form and dislikes a disagreeable form; he dwells without mindfulness of the body, with a limited mind. He does not truly understand the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, where those evil, unwholesome states cease without remainder. Thus, for him, with regard to bodily contact, whatever feeling arises — pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — he rejoices in that feeling, welcomes it, and remains attached to it. Because he rejoices, welcomes, and is attached to that feeling, delight arises. Having delight in those feelings, he is attached. With attachment as condition, existence arises; with existence as condition, birth arises; with birth as condition, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Thus is the origination of this whole mass of suffering.

title: Elder Nisabha: Having abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure, Those truly delightful things that please the mind, With faith, I went forth to make…
content:
Elder Nisabha:

Having abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure,
Those truly delightful things that please the mind,
With faith, I went forth to make an end of suffering.

I do not delight in death, I do not delight in life.
I await the time, mindful and clearly comprehending.

title: Elder Sunāga: Skilled in the mind's sign, knowing the taste of seclusion, Meditating, mindful, careful, he attains non-worldly happiness.
content:
Elder Sunāga:

Skilled in the mind's sign, knowing the taste of seclusion,
Meditating, mindful, careful, he attains non-worldly happiness.

title: What do you think, Ambattha? Have you heard the brahmins who are elders, senior, teachers, and ancestors say? In the past, those ascetics among the…
content: What do you think, Ambattha? Have you heard the brahmins who are elders, senior, teachers, and ancestors say? In the past, those ascetics among the brahmins, the authors of the mantras, the reciters of the mantras who sang, spoke, and compiled the sacred verses that today's brahmins sing, speak, and recite just as the former ones did. Those ascetics named Atthaka, Vāmaka, ..., Kassapa, Bhagu. Did they bathe well, groom well, keep their hair and beard well-trimmed, adorn themselves with garlands and jewels, wear white clothes, enjoy and indulge in the five strands of sensual pleasure, as you and your teacher do now?

title: There are these five ways of removing resentment, bhikkhus, by which any resentment that arises in a bhikkhu should be fully removed. What five? Toward…
content: There are these five ways of removing resentment, bhikkhus, by which any resentment that arises in a bhikkhu should be fully removed. What five? Toward whomever resentment arises, loving-kindness should be developed toward that person. Thus resentment toward that person should be removed. Toward whomever resentment arises, compassion should be developed toward that person. Thus resentment toward that person should be removed. Toward whomever resentment arises, equanimity should be developed toward that person. Thus resentment toward that person should be removed. Toward whomever resentment arises, non-attention and non-reflection should be practiced regarding that person. Thus resentment toward that person should be removed. Toward whomever resentment arises, the fact of one's own kamma should be established: 'The venerable one is the owner of his kamma, heir to his kamma, born of his kamma, related to his kamma, supported by his kamma. Whatever kamma he does, whether good or evil, he will be the heir of that kamma.' Thus resentment toward that person should be removed. These, bhikkhus, are the five ways of removing resentment by which any resentment that arises in a bhikkhu should be fully removed.

title: Elder Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja: Living this life is not without its rules, But food does not come close to the heart. Because there is food, the…
content:
Elder Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja:

Living this life is not without its rules,
But food does not come close to the heart.
Because there is food, the body survives.
Seeing this, I wander seeking food.

The wise have experienced that it is truly a mire.
Homage and offerings come from families.
Like a subtle arrow, hard to draw out,
So for a fool, honor is hard to abandon.

title: Elder Nun Somā: That state hard to attain, Only sages attain it. With two-finger wisdom, a woman — How could she hope to attain it?…
content:
Elder Nun Somā:

That state hard to attain,
Only sages attain it.
With two-finger wisdom, a woman —
How could she hope to attain it?

What does womanhood matter
When the mind is well concentrated,
When wisdom unfolds,
Rightly seeing the sublime Dhamma?

Everywhere, delight is destroyed,
The mass of delusion is shattered.
Know thus, Evil One!
You are Death, you are defeated.

title: Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has a slight illness. He thinks: 'Now this slight illness has arisen in me; there is reason to lie down. Let…
content:
Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has a slight illness. He thinks: 'Now this slight illness has arisen in me; there is reason to lie down. Let me lie down.' He lies down, not making an effort... unrealized. Bhikkhus, this is the seventh ground for laziness.
Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has just recovered from an illness, not long recovered. He thinks: 'I have just recovered from an illness, not long recovered. My body is weak due to illness and cannot bear it. Let me lie down.' He lies down, not making an effort... unrealized. Bhikkhus, this is the eighth ground for laziness.

title: Elder Nhātakamuni: Afflicted by a wind disease, you live in the deep forest, With limited alms-gathering, lean and weak. What will a bhikkhu do with…
content:
Elder Nhātakamuni:

Afflicted by a wind disease, you live in the deep forest,
With limited alms-gathering, lean and weak.
What will a bhikkhu do with such a body?

My body is flooded with spreading joy and bliss.
Even though lean, I will live in the forest.

Developing the seven factors of enlightenment,
The five faculties and the five powers,
Possessing subtle jhāna, I live without taints.

Freed from the fetters, mind pure, unstained,
Always, well contemplating, I live without taints.

All taints, internal and external, that were previously in me —
All are cut off, they will not arise again.

The five aggregates are fully understood,
They stand with roots cut off.
The end of suffering is attained; now there is no more renewed existence.

title: - Venerable Sāriputta, what is happiness and what is suffering? - Venerable sir, birth is suffering, non-birth is happiness. When there is birth, venerable sir,…
content:
- Venerable Sāriputta, what is happiness and what is suffering?
- Venerable sir, birth is suffering, non-birth is happiness. When there is birth, venerable sir, this suffering is to be expected: cold, heat, hunger, thirst, defecation, urination, contact with fire, contact with rod, contact with sword. Even relatives and friends, when they meet and gather, cause distress. Venerable sir, birth is suffering; when there is birth, this suffering is to be expected. When there is no birth, venerable sir, this happiness is to be expected: no cold, no heat, no hunger, no thirst, no defecation, no urination, no contact with fire, no contact with rod, no contact with sword. Even relatives and friends, when they meet and gather, cause no distress. Venerable sir, when there is no birth, this happiness is to be expected.
